editorialSummary.heading: What Plano ISD families should know for 2026-2027
paragraphs: Plano ISD lists 171 instructional days for 2026-2027: 82 in the first semester and 89 in the second. The first grading period ends October 9. Students then have no classes October 12–16 and return October 19 for the second grading period.

Students are also off November 3. For Thanksgiving week, the text calendar labels November 23–27 as Thanksgiving Break, while the graphic calendar separately marks November 23–24 as Professional Learning Trade Days and November 25–27 as Thanksgiving Break. Either way, students have no classes all five weekdays.

December 18 is an early-release day and the end of the first semester. Official Winter Break runs December 21–January 1, followed by a separate student holiday on January 4; classes resume January 5. Students are also off February 15–16, March 15–19 for Spring Break, and March 26 and 29.

May 21 is the final student day and an early-release day. Plano ISD’s text calendar also lists regular hours by school level. On district early-release days, elementary schools dismiss at 12:00 p.m., while Beaty, Isaacs, Pearson, and Head Start dismiss at 11:55 a.m. Secondary schools follow separate exam-dismissal schedules.

faqs.question: When is the first day of school for Plano ISD in 2026-2027?
faqs.answer: The first day for students is Tuesday, August 11, 2026.

faqs.question: What is the last day of school for Plano ISD?
faqs.answer: The final student day is Friday, May 21, 2027. It is an early-release day and the end of both the second semester and fourth grading period.

faqs.question: How many instructional days are on the calendar?
faqs.answer: Plano ISD lists 171 instructional days for every grade level: 82 days in the first semester and 89 in the second.

faqs.question: What are the regular Plano ISD school hours?
faqs.answer: Elementary schools run 7:40 a.m.-3:00 p.m., middle schools 8:25 a.m.-3:45 p.m., and high and senior high schools 9:05 a.m.-4:30 p.m.

faqs.question: What hours do full-day Pre-K and Head Start follow?
faqs.answer: Beaty, Isaacs, Pearson, and Head Start run 7:55 a.m.-3:15 p.m. Full-day Pre-K programs at the other campuses named in the text calendar run 7:40 a.m.-3:00 p.m.

faqs.question: Does Guinn Special Programs Center use different hours?
faqs.answer: Yes. Guinn’s K-5 schedule is 7:40 a.m.-3:00 p.m., while grades 6-12 attend from 8:30 a.m.-4:00 p.m.

faqs.question: Does Plano ISD have a fall break in October 2026?
faqs.answer: Students have no classes October 12–16, 2026, but Plano ISD does not label the full week as one official Fall Break. The graphic calendar marks October 12–14 as Student/Teacher Holidays, October 15 as a Staff Day/Student Holiday, and October 16 as a Campus PLC Day/Student Holiday. The text calendar groups October 15–16 as Student Holiday / Staff Development / Work Days. Students return October 19.

faqs.question: Is November 3 a school day for students?
faqs.answer: No. Tuesday, November 3, is a student holiday while staff development and work time are scheduled.

faqs.question: What dates are included in Thanksgiving Break?
faqs.answer: Students are off November 23–27, 2026, and return Monday, November 30. The text calendar calls all five days Thanksgiving Break; the graphic calendar labels November 23–24 as Professional Learning Trade Days and November 25–27 as Thanksgiving Break.

faqs.question: When is Plano ISD Winter Break in 2026-27?
faqs.answer: Official Winter Break runs December 21, 2026, through January 1, 2027. January 4 is a separate student holiday and staff day, so students return Tuesday, January 5.

faqs.question: When does the second semester begin?
faqs.answer: The second semester begins Tuesday, January 5, 2027. That date also starts the third grading period.

faqs.question: Is Martin Luther King Jr. Day a district holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes. Monday, January 18, is a student and teacher holiday.

faqs.question: Are students off on February 15 and 16?
faqs.answer: Yes. Both February 15 and 16, 2027, are student holidays. The graphic calendar labels February 15 as a staff day/student holiday and February 16 as a Campus PLC day/student holiday; the text calendar groups both as staff development/work days. Students return February 17.

faqs.question: When is Spring Break in 2027?
faqs.answer: Spring Break runs March 15-19, 2027. Students return Monday, March 22, for the beginning of the fourth grading period.

faqs.question: Are Plano ISD students off March 26–29, 2027?
faqs.answer: Students have no classes Friday, March 26, or Monday, March 29. With the weekend between them, that creates a four-day stretch away from school. The district lists the two weekdays as separate calendar events. Classes resume March 30.

faqs.question: Which dates are early-release days?
faqs.answer: The district lists Friday, December 18, 2026, and Friday, May 21, 2027. Both dates also close a semester and grading period.

faqs.question: What time do elementary and early childhood students leave on early-release days?
faqs.answer: Elementary schools dismiss at 12:00 p.m. Beaty, Isaacs, Pearson, and Head Start dismiss at 11:55 a.m.

faqs.question: What are the secondary exam dismissal times?
faqs.answer: High and senior high schools release at 1:10 p.m., and Academy High School releases at 1:30 p.m. Middle schools release at 12:40 p.m. on the last day of exams only.

faqs.question: When are Plano ISD’s four grading periods, and how many instructional days are in each?
faqs.answer: The grading periods run August 11–October 9 (43 instructional days), October 19–December 18 (39), January 5–March 12 (46), and March 22–May 21 (43). Together they total 171 instructional days: 82 in the first semester and 89 in the second.

faqs.question: When are Plano ISD graduation dates in 2027?
faqs.answer: The 2026-2027 text calendar lists Academy High School and senior high school graduations as TBD; it does not give ceremony dates. Confirm current ceremony information with Plano ISD.

faqs.question: Do the faith acknowledgement symbols mean school is closed?
faqs.answer: No. The symbols identify religious observances, not automatic school closures. Check whether a date is separately marked as a student holiday or schedule change.

faqs.question: Where can parents download the official calendars?
faqs.answer: Use the graphic and text PDF links on this page or visit the Plano ISD calendar page for current versions and later-year formats.

faqs.question: Can Plano ISD change these dates or dismissal times?
faqs.answer: Yes. The approved graphic says the calendar is subject to change. Families should confirm campus exam schedules, transportation changes, and revised dates through official district or school messages.

about.dataSource: This page combines Plano ISD’s official 2026-2027 graphic calendar with its English text calendar dated April 20, 2026. Student attendance dates, graphic labels and grading-period arrows were checked against the text calendar’s event list, regular hours, early-release and exam-dismissal schedules, and instructional-day totals.
about.processing: Student events follow official labels and ranges. October 12–14, October 15, October 16, Winter Break, January 4, February 15, February 16, March 26 and March 29 are separate events; breaks preserve the combined student no-school periods for family planning. Thanksgiving week follows the text calendar, with the graphic calendar’s trade-day labels noted separately. Early-release notes distinguish elementary/listed early-childhood dismissal from secondary exam schedules, including the middle-school last-exam-day restriction. Faith acknowledgements and staff-only dates before the first student day are excluded because they do not change regular-year attendance. Events and key dates use field-level provenance rather than an object-wide basis: official means a directly printed date, label or range; derived includes normalized names, internal event classifications and attendance-status mappings, as well as calendar relationships. Grading-period end dates and day counts cite the text calendar; start boundaries follow the graphic calendar’s grading-period arrows and ranges. Event notes are editorial paraphrases or source comparisons, so they use noteBasis=derived and cite their supporting official documents in noteSourceIds. October 16 and February 16 staff-label differences are recorded in sourceDiscrepancies without changing student attendance dates. The graphic grading-period legend is not an event-specific officialLabel.
about.updates: Plano ISD publishes graphic and text calendar formats. This page follows the reviewed 2026-2027 documents; later-year files and any revised schedules require separate verification.
about.disclaimer: This independent reference is not operated by Plano ISD. Families should confirm exam-day dismissal, transportation, parent conferences, weather changes, graduation dates, and campus-specific updates with the district or their child’s school.

statistics.label: Total no-school weekdays
statistics.explanation: Counted from published no-class events between the first and last student days. Weekends and shortened school days are excluded, and overlapping events count once.

statistics.label: Student no-school days
statistics.explanation: Counts weekdays without regular classes outside holidays and multi-day breaks, including staff or planning days. Overlapping entries count once.

statistics.label: Listed early-release dates
statistics.explanation: Counted from early-release entries on this calendar. An early-release date still counts as a student attendance day.

statistics.label: Longest listed break
statistics.explanation: Dec 19, 2026–Jan 4, 2027, including weekends. The stretch contains 11 confirmed no-school weekdays.

statistics.label: Long weekends
statistics.explanation: Counts three- or four-day no-school stretches formed by a weekend plus one or two confirmed weekday closures. Longer school breaks are excluded.

statistics.label: Full-week breaks
statistics.explanation: Counts continuous no-school stretches containing at least five confirmed weekdays without regular classes. Adjacent holidays and weekends remain part of the same break.
